reports.title: Lake Maumelle fishing report
reports.text:
Black bass fishing is fair. The largemouths are fair in 10-20 feet depth. Try using Carolina rigs, jigs, drop-shots and crankbaits. Spotted bass (aka Kentucky bass) also are fair and being found in 10-20 feet mixed in with the largemouths. Try using drop-shot, jigs and cranks. In this week’s Tuesday night bass tournament, Cody Bryant and Brad Lequieu brought in a five-bass stringer totaling 15.29 pounds to win. Ben Burke and Randall Clark were helped by the Big Bass of 4.63 pounds and were second with 14.97 pounds total.
Crappie fishing is good. The last report said they are off of the banks and scattered around brush and rock piles 15-20 fee. Try using jigs.

reports.text:

reports.title: Lake Charles fishing report
reports.text:

Spoon main lake points for walleye and let a plastic worm drop off the ledge at about 12 feet for black bass – mostly Kentuckies but they are nice sized. The stripers are going deeper and when you see a topwater bite early it is bass, while the stripers are under that at about 50-60 feet – drop a spoon on their heads.

reports.title: Lake Maumelle fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are fair. Reports of the bass being found in a wide range of depths. They can be found shallow, some are starting to hit topwater as well as in 16-20 feet depth. Try using crankbaits, flukes, wacky rig shallow and Texas rig deep. Spotted (Kentucky) bass are fair, with reports of them being found deep, at around 16-20 feet. Shaky heads are your best bet for the spot action. Twenty-six boats went out in the Tuesday night black bass tournament this week, and 14 caught limits. Cameron Nesterenko and Andrew Wooley caught 12.94 bass to win, edging Billy Wright and Allen Ward’s 12.61 pounds, though Billy and Allen brought in the Big Bass of 4.70 pounds.

Some of the crappie are in the 2-pound range, and two cats that were pulled from the lake this week “were the biggest I’ve seen,” she said. “We’ve been going through crickets like crazy for the bream and the crappie.” Black bass are biting “pretty good” on jigs and minnows. Crappie are also biting minnows and white jigs.
(updated 6-15-2023) Ken Winstead at Whiskers Sporting Goods (501-889-2011) in Perryville said the crappie bite continues to be typical for the continuous water changes due to weather, so move around from shallow to deep…

reports.title: Spring River fishing report
reports.text: Smallmouth bass are hitting but have been tough the last few weeks. “This is the time to chase smallies, and we have been so busy with chasing bows, we have not done many trips for smallies, but that should ramp up this month. The smallmouth bass is the native fish of the Spring River and local creeks. Hard to beat skull head Sculpin patterns; heavy-weighted Woollies in olive, brown and black work well; and Clousers. Got to get it to the bottom and work it slow. “The canoe hatch is on every Saturday on the river now. Saturday is not a great day to fish, but through the week and on Sundays it’s perfect. The canoe hatch will be heavy on Saturdays until September. “Be safe wading the river is…

reports.text:
The following techniques will give anglers a chance at catching numbers of rainbow trout, walleye, crappie, bream and white bass that have received little fishing pressure this season:
The crappie spawn is nearing an end, but these fish can be caught with live minnows and jigs fished in current breaks around sandbars and rock structure. Crappie shy away from heavy current and thrive in protected areas out of the main flow.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Maumelle fishing report
reports.text:
For the week, largemouth bass have ranged from good to fair. Reports of the bass being found on points around 10 feet deep. Their black bass cousins, the spotted bass (Kentucky bass), were great over the weekend and the beginning this week before slowing back down. In WestRock’s Tuesday night weekly black bass tournament this week, Matt Hedrick and Brandon Crain caught 14.39 pounds on a five-bass stringer to win, and the top three finishers were at or over 12.4 pounds. Robert and Tracy White hauled in the Big Bass of 4.35 pounds.
Crappie, though, were good. Reports of crappie hanging in the brush around 18 feet of water.

* Largemouth bass remain fair to good, best early and late, ranging from 2-3 pounds in 3-8 feet of water on flats near vegetation, and others in 6- to 10-feet-deep creek channels where grass and reeds and fresh lily pad shoots are emerging. Buzzbaits, plastic frogs, Bass Assassin Shads, Bill Lewis Lures StutterSteps, SB-57 squarebills, Echo 1.75 Crankbaits and 10-inch Power Worms are working. reports.text: Crappie are fair and have retreated back to deeper water; use minnows and jigs. Black bass were poor this week.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Horseshoe Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Kent Williams of Oxbow Guide Service (870-278-7978) said crappie are in their summer pattern.
No reports on catfish or bass.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Catherine fishing report
reports.text:
With the heavy currents in the river, bass have been pushed into points and pockets and are holding close to structure and cover. Topwater is starting to come into its own but with the large amount of forage in the water it takes a ton of casts to fill a limit of 12-inch bass. Bigger bass have been caught but the tournament weights are on a downward swing. Also, for some reason, bass also like the white swim jig.
No crappie report.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Charles fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are in the same areas and are biting well on minnows and jigs. Black bass are good, with a plastic worm working best. Bass are being caught around brush and rocky points.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Nimrod fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good and being caught about 8-10 feet deep on minnows as well as jigs in chartreuse with a gold willow leaf skirt. Black bass are good, with green pumpkin colored worms working best. Your best success will come on the shoreline in the grass with the higher water giving bass more areas for habitat.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Sequoyah fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are hanging in there, with fair catches report using minnows and jigs. A few crappie are still being caught shallow, they report. Black bass are off and on.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Millwood Lake fishing report
reports.text:
* Largemouth bass: They were fair early in the morning, and slowing down after 9-11 a.m. with fluctuating pool levels, on chartreuse Sexy Shad colored buzzbaits and hatterbaits. The juvenile and adolescent bass, about 10-15 inches, seemed to be the most aggressive. Black Grape, Junebug Red or Black/Blue tail 10-inch worms have been working for some bass over the past several weeks if you could find some decent water clarity in backs of the oxbows away from Little River current. Largemouths were slower in responding this past week. A few bass were caught last week on Horny Toads and Yum Tip Toads 4-8 feet deep in the pads and grass.
No reports on white bass or crappie.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Peckerwood Lake fishing report
reports.text: Crappie have been working for anglers trolling, with fair results using minnows or jigs. Black bass are good on jigs.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Maumelle fishing report
reports.text:
WestRock Landing in Roland (501-658-5598) reported Thursday that with the rising water the crappie bite has picked back up with excellent results this week. Reports came in of the crappie being found 18-20 feet deep above structure.
Meanwhile, largemouth bass are fair. Some can be found in the grass on the banks and around the grass in 8-12 feet biting a variety of lures. Try using crankbaits, spinnerbaits and swimbaits. The largemouths’ black bass brethren, the spotted bass (Kentucky bass) also are fair. Some anglers report finding them near drop-offs around 16-20 feet and off rocky banks. Try using jigs for the spots. Reflective these opinions on the black bass bite, the Tuesday night…

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Beaver Tailwater fishing report
reports.text: Also, try fishing around brush for bluegill and crappie when the water is like this. Kentucky bass are being caught early morning, along chunk rock and around structure.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Catherine fishing report
reports.text: With the heavy currents in the river, Bass have been pushed into points and pockets and are holding close to structure and cover. Top water is starting to come into its own but with the large amount of forage in the water it takes a ton of casts to fill a limit of 12 inch Bass. Bigger bass have been caught but the tournament weights are on a downward swing. Also, for some reason Bass also like the white swim jig. No Crappie report.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Hamilton fishing report
reports.text: Bass have been fair at best over the last couple weeks. The rainwater has washed a ton of food into the lake and the Bass will not chase baits.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Maumelle fishing report
reports.text:
WestRock Landing in Roland (501-658-5598) reported Thursday that with the rising water the crappie bite has picked back up with excellent results this week. Reports came in of the crappie being found 18-20 feet deep above structure.
Meanwhile, largemouth bass are fair. Some can be found in the grass on the banks and around the grass in 8-12 feet biting a variety of lures. Try using crankbaits, spinnerbaits and swimbaits. The largemouths’ black bass brethren, the spotted bass (Kentucky bass) also are fair. Some anglers report finding them near drop-offs around 16-20 feet and off rocky banks. Try using jigs for the spots.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Beaver Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Crappie are moving and can be caught from shallow to suspended in 40 feet of water. Bass have been good.
Crappie also have picked up; use minnows or jigs. Black bass are good for anglers who were using swimbaits, worms and small soft plastics.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Bull Shoals Lake fishing report
reports.text: Smallmouth bass are mostly in mid-lake area; anglers should target long points and sunken humps and islands.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: DeGray Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Crappie (my thing) are definitely in the brushpiles above the thermocline.
(update 6-3-2021) Local crappie angler Charles Abernathy said, “I fished a lot over Memorial Day weekend with my family. We caught some good sized crappie on 1/16-ounce jigs (hand ties/Bobby Garland/Mr. Crappie Slab Slangers).
This time of year, a crappie fisherman has multiple patterns to choose from (like most seasons). I treat my crappie fishing a lot like deer hunting. Most folks don’t tear off through the woods like a silverback gorilla while slip hunting deer haha … maybe crappie fishing should be approached the same way…slow and steady.
DeGray is full of timber and it’s no surprise, a crappie can be caught on…

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Catherine fishing report
reports.text: Bass are still on beds in Catherine in the cooler areas. Bedded bass will take a jig if worked correctly, and some monsters have been boated lately. Bass are transitioning to the summer patterns with many seeking cooler temps on main lake points or rocky areas next to current. No crappie report.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Charles fishing report
reports.text: Shelly Jeffrey at Lake Charles State Park (870-878-6595) said Lake Charles anglers and visitors enjoyed a beautiful, cool Memorial Day weekend, and she received lots of fishing reports on bream and catfish, with a few nice bass caught and some good activity seen with crappie. Crappie are good. Crappie are being caught around brushpiles, stumps and rocky points. Black bass are good, with anglers using spinnerbaits, crankbaits and plastic worms.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Hamilton fishing report
reports.text: Bass continue to be sluggish with the summer transition happening. Topwater walking baits, swim jigs and crankbaits in shad presentations do a great job at being breakfast for bass on rocky main lake points and backwater flats points until the sun sits high. No crappie reports.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Sequoyah fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair on minnows and jigs. Black bass are fair, with topwater baits working the best.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Millwood Lake fishing report
reports.text:
* Largemouth bass: slow to fair this week with falling pool levels, on Black/blue or Chartreuse Shad buzzbaits and Chatterbaits. Juvenile Bass from 12-14 inches seemed to be the most aggressive. Black grape or solid black, 10″ power worms have been working for a few Bass over the past couple weeks. Largemouths were slower responsive, this past week.
Pitching a Bass Assassin Jingle Bug in black/blue tail, or Okeechobee Craw colors got a few reactions on stumps in 8-10 feet deep a few days ago. Bass Assassin Shad jerkbaits got a few reactions, early in the morning and best color we got reactions continue to be the pumpkin seed-chartreuse tail, and Black Shad in the 5″ sizes. The Chatterbaits…

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Brewer Lake fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good on size 6 minnows and on jigs. Black bass a good and favor the size 12 bass minnows as well as goldfish. Catfishing is good using live baits such as nightcrawlers, goldfish on the trotlines, and bass minnows.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Cane Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bream activity has remained steady with the bream being caught with crickets, while crappie are being caught with jigs and minnows.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Beaverfork fishing report
reports.text:
Water level has been above normal and somewhat clear, the bite has slowed for the past week or so; BUT, Dennis says he caught a few bass who were schooling right before and during the rain.
For bass, he says the bite has slowed over the past two weeks. Water temperature is around 75 degrees and the crappie are slow in mid-level water; use floating lures with dive, as well as jigs. Bass are slow and in the shallows and in the grass. Dennis says he caught several on bass baits where bass lurk.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fayetteville fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair on minnows and jigs. Black bass improved over the week with good catches on topwater lures.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Bear Creek Lake/Storm Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Tyler Ball, park ranger at Mississippi River State Park (870-295-4040), said anglers at Bear Creek Lake report having great success in catching crappie and blue catfish within the last week. Crappie have been reported to be biting at depths of 3-4 feet, particularly in coves.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Charles fishing report
reports.text: Bass, she added, were hitting topwater baits, and bass hauls were good. Crappie are also following along with the bream by going after worms and brightly colored jigs, with good results.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Arkansas River fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are good around the jetties and are hitting chartreuse/black square-bills, the back Bandit 200 Series, and a black/blue chatterbait in the backwaters.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Beaver Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Crappie are being caught trolling cranks and with jigs. Bass are early and late hitting on top and drifting deeper as the day moves on. Catfish are good and Jon said he’s had lots of reports of catfish at night being caught on black spinnerbaits throughout the lake by nighttime bass fisherman.
Crappie are fair for anglers who made the switch to crankbaits this week. Black bass appear to be spawning, and it’s a hodgepodge on the type of baits anglers were catching them on.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Brewer Lake fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good in 10-12 feet depth over the underwater brush; fish them with minnows or jigs. Black bass are good; topwater lures, jigs and minnows have been working well.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Buffalo National River/Crooked Creek fishing report
reports.text: LEFT: Young Porter Fugitt noodled this Ozark bass on the Buffalo River last week.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Bull Shoals Lake fishing report
reports.text: Berkley Wake Bait for smallies and Kentucky bass on the main and secondary points, along with the sunken islands, hump, bluff and bluff ends. Smallmouth bass are being caught around the gravel banks, boat ramps and old roads – good places to drag baits like the Ned rig, Hula Grubs, Tubes, the Lil’ McMinnow or Carolina rigs from 18-32 feet down.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Crown Lake fishing report
reports.text: Crappie reports are poor. Black bass are good late in the evenings and early mornings in shallow water; use your favorite topwater bait.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: DeGray Lake fishing report
reports.text: Black bass reports say topwater early, Chug Bug, Whopper Plopper and Zara Spook. Crappie can still be pulled out of some of the brushpiles between 12 and 18 feet, but most important is the thermocline – stay above it.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Greers Ferry Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Black bass are super shallow to 40 feet – they are chasing bream shallow, to eating crawdads deep, and all in between with a lot of different baits working. Crappie are as good as always, in and around any wood or manmade structure on jigs and minnows in 12-30 feet of water.
Smallmouth bass are responding well to Carolina rigs and Whopper Ploppers at the lower end of the lake. Largemouth bass are prominent in the upper end of the lake, actively biting the Horny Toad in the early mornings.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Harris Brake Lake fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good, though they have moved to deeper areas. Black bass are good.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Catherine (Below Carpenter Dam) fishing report
reports.text: Anglers casting jigs in gray or white around rocks and sandbars have caught decent numbers of bass when the turbines are running.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fayetteville fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are still good despite the rising temps, and the crappie are hanging out at 10-12 feet. No reports came in on black bass.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Maumelle fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are slow, biting best at dusk and at dawn on swimbaits, jigs, Alabama rigs and spinnerbaits. Crappie are fair in about 16-18 feet of water, biting on minnows and jigs. Update Friday, June 26: They report that crappie good today from 20-22 feet deep, and they received a few good crappie reports this morning.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Nimrod fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good, with anglers having best success fishing in 20 feet of water with the crappie suspended at 12 feet. Black bass are good on topwater baits, Chug Bugs and worms.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Norrell fishing report
reports.text: Crappie have moved back out deep and are biting fair on No. Bass fishing has been good early and late in the day as well as at night.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ouachita fishing report
reports.text:
LEFt: 16-year-old Sarah Bailey of Malvern marvels at the mess of big crappie she caught recently at Lake Ouachita.
Todd Gadberry at Mountain Harbor Resort and Spa (870-867-2191/800-832-2276 out of state) reports that black bass are fair. Crappie remain good.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Sequoyah fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are in a hiding mode now with very few caught. Black bass are good on plastic worms and buzzbaits.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Winona fishing report
reports.text: Crappie have been slow to bite but some are still being caught on No. Bass are biting in the mornings and evenings on floating or Carolina-rigged plastics, topwater baits, buzzbaits and spinnerbaits.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Millwood Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Millwood Lake received 55,000 Florida bass fingerlings stocked last week by AGFC. Current information indicates another 245,000 Florida bass fingerlings are yet to be added this year year by AGFC hatchery personnel for a total of around 300,000 Florida bass.
* Largemouth bass: Soft plastic jerk baits like Bass Assassin Shads, soft plastic frogs, Ken Pops and Pop Rs are seeing good reactions with the lake back at normal pool. Most largemouths are active at night and at early daybreak for a few hours in the oxbows of McGuire, Mud and Horseshoe lakes.
Texas-rigged Trick & Twitch Worms are working near cypress trees and knees drawing a fair response from lethargic bass from 8-12 feet deep.
*…

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Saline River Access in Benton fishing report
reports.text: Lisa Spencer at Lisa’s Bait Shop (501-778-6944) says bass fishing has been good on the river with minnows, plastic worms, lizards and Brush Hogs or small crawdad crankbaits. Crappie are hitting No.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Sunset Lake fishing report
reports.text: Crappie fishing has been slow but some are still catching a few early in the mornings on pink minnows. Bass have been hitting wacky rigged plastics, chatterbaits, buzzbaits and live minnows.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: War Eagle Creek/Beaver Lake Area fishing report
reports.text: Loy Lewis with War Eagle Creek Outfitting (479-530-3262) said fishing going great on War Eagle Creek for smallmouth bass; they are biting about all day, he said. Good Kentucky bass are being caught close to rock ledges on points.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Peckerwood Lake fishing report
reports.text: Crappie have fallen off; poor results this week. Black bass are good; no baits were suggested by the anglers.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Spring River fishing report
reports.text: Smallmouth have been biting well this week, Mark says.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Craig D. Campbell Lake Conway Reservoir fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair on minnows and jigs. Black bass are good; spinnerbaits, crankbaits, plastic worms, topwater baits, regular worms and frogs were all getting hits regularly.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Arkansas River fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good; focus on 8-10 feet depth with a Roadrunner, or look to 10 feet with a Beaver Bottom bait. Bass reports are good.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Beaver Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Crappie are fair. Bass are schooling, with some topwater noted early.
Crappie are fair; they’re being caught in deep waters now with minnows. Black bass are good on spinnerbaits and topwaters, as well as with drop-shot and jigs.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Bishop Park Ponds fishing report
reports.text: Crappie been slow, but a few were caught off of crappie minnows and black/ chartreuse Bobby Garland Jigs. Bass have been hitting minnows and black salties.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Brewer Lake fishing report
reports.text: Crappie also are good still. Black bass are hitting on top in the middle of the day, and the catch totals are good.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Bull Shoals Lake fishing report
reports.text: Smaller Kentucky bass are out on main and secondary points, bluffs and bluff ends and being caught on swimbaits or jerkbaits near shad balls on cloudy and windy days. For smallmouth, the gravel banks, boat ramps and old roads are good places to drag baits like the Ned rig, Hula Grubs Tubes, the Lil McMinnow or Carolina rigs 18-32 feet down.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: DeGray Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Darryl Morris at Family Fishing Trips (501-844-5418) says, “S urface water temp is 64 degrees and some crappie are still hanging around the brushpiles but more and more finicky on the bite.
Bass are being caught early on topwaters and buzzbaits. Crappie are still being caught in the brushpiles.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Greers Ferry Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Crappie are still eating well in outside bushes, over brushpiles and in pole timber on jigs and minnows 15-30 feet. Black bass are eating on top down to 30 feet and all in between on a variety of baits and techniques.
(updated 6-17-2020) Fish ’N Stuff (501-834-5733) in Sherwood says largemouth and smallmouth bass are hitting topwaters early in the morning and late in the evening, while the best fishing in the middle of the day is focusing on 20-25 feet depth with a Carolina rig.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Harris Brake Lake fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are now in the deep areas of the lake, but catch results have been good. Black bass are good fishing on the shoreline with spinnerbaits or throwing a topwater.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Catherine (Below Carpenter Dam) fishing report
reports.text: Fishermen casting jigs in grey or white around rocks and sand bars have caught decent numbers of bass when the turbines are running.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Charles fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good. Brushpiles, stumpy areas and rocky points are turning out the crappie. The bass bite is good on spinnerbaits and crankbaits.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fayetteville fishing report
reports.text: Crappie have been fair; catches are coming in 10-12 feet depth. Black bass are good.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Norrell fishing report
reports.text: Lisa Spencer at Lisa’s Bait Shop (501-778-6944) said crappie have been slow, but the best bet is fishing deep with crappie minnows and Bobby Garland Jigs. Bass are being caught off of chatterbaits, plastics and spinnerbaits.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ouachita fishing report
reports.text: Todd Gadberry at Mountain Harbor Resort and Spa (870-867-2191/800-832-2276 out of state) reports that black bass are fair to good. Crappie are still good.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Sequoyah fishing report
reports.text: Crappie, though, have been hard to locate now and results have been poor. Black bass are good on spinnerbaits and buzzbaits.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Winona fishing report
reports.text: Lisa Spencer at Lisa’s Bait Shop (501-778-6944) said crappie are good on crappie minnows. Bass are being caught off of black salties, spinnerbaits and crankbaits.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Millwood Lake fishing report
reports.text:
* Largemouth bass: Soft plastic jerk baits like Bass Assassin Shads, soft plastic frogs, Ken Pops, and Pop R’s are seeing good reactions with the lake back at normal pool. Most Largemouths are active at night and at early daybreak for a few hours, in the oxbows of McGuire, Mud, and Horseshoe Lakes.
Bass Assassin Shads, and soft plastic frogs are still getting the best responses at dawn, from 2-5 feet of depth around stumps, lily pads, and bushes. The Bass Assassin Shads continue working near lily pads at dawn, and near cover, grass, and stumps, for the past couple weeks.
Texas-rigged Trick & Twitch worms are working near cypress trees and knees drawing a fair response from lethargic…

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Saline River Access in Benton fishing report
reports.text: Lisa Spencer at Lisa’s Bait Shop (501-778-6944) says trotlines been good baited up with goldfish and black salties catching catfish and bass. A few crappie are being caught off of Kalin’s Tennessee Shad-colored Jigs and crappie minnows fishing some of the deeper holes.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Sunset Lake fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are slow but will bite crappie minnows. Bass have been hitting on beetle spins, crankbaits and Zoom Trick Worms rigged wacky style.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Beaver Tailwater fishing report
reports.text: Due to the warm water conditions, smallmouth bass are being caught further up the tailwaters.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Bishop Park Ponds fishing report
reports.text: Lisa Spencer at Lisa’s Bait Shop (501-778-6944) says bass are hitting live minnows, topwater baits and floating worms. Crappie have been biting fair on pink or No.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Norfork Lake fishing report
reports.text:
“ Largemouth, smallmouth and spotted bass have been in the same areas as striped bass early in the morning. When the bass go down, work the shoreline out to 30 feet of water. The bass seem to be hanging at the top of the sunken brush.
Crappie are also scattered out from the old shoreline up to near the new shoreline. Small grubs tipped with a crappie minnow have been picking up a few fish. There is a lot of brush under the water, so the crappie have lots of places to feed.”

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Arkansas River fishing report
reports.text: The University of Arkansas at Pine Bluff Bass Fishing Team said water temperature is in the upper 70s. Black bass were biting fairly well off of large woody cover and along the steeper rock banks where morning shad spawns were active in Lake Langhofer.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: White Oak Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass fishing is fair.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Craig D. Campbell Lake Conway Reservoir fishing report
reports.text: Crappie reports are fair. Black bass are good on spinnerbaits and topwater baits.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Beaver Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Crappie are starting to school up at and around 20 feet deep. Bass are schooled up and, again, use your sonar and look off main points in 20-30 feet of water. Side note: Nighttime under lights is starting to work on crappie and white bass in and around the Highway 12 bridge.
Crappie have been poor; best opportunity to catch them is trolling and spider-rigging. Black bass are good on flukes and Senkos during the day, and using topwater/plastics/spinnerbaits in the early morning and late evenings.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Bishop Park Ponds fishing report
reports.text: A few crappie were caught off of pink and regular crappie minnows. Bass are good off of live crawdads and beetle spins.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Brewer Lake fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good. Black bass are good. Catfish are good on trotline bait and big goldfish, as well as size 20 bass minnows.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Bull Shoals Lake fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are going after jerkbaits near shad balls; they like spinnerbaits and chatterbaits on the old banks and bushes with stain. For smallmouth bass, the gravel banks, boat ramps and old roads are good places to drag baits like the Ned rig, Hula Grubs Tubes, the little McMinnow or Carolina rigs from 18-32 feet down.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: DeGray Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Darryl Morris at Family Fishing Trips says, “ Believe it or not, we are still catching crappie from 6 feet to 15 feet deep on brushpiles using live bait when the water temp is 82-degrees.
Black bass are kinda slow as expected. Crappie are still in the brushpiles around the mid-teens.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Greers Ferry Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Crappie catching continues to be good in and around bushes and now out to pole timber and brushpiles from super shallow out to 25 feet on jigs and minnows. Black bass are chewing well with shad spawns and just plain eating after their spawns, on a variety of baits in a variety of places.
(updated 6-10-2020) Fish ’N Stuff (501-834-5733) in Sherwood says bass are being caught on a 3/8-ounce salmon craw in about 15 feet of water. Crappie can be caught trolling on Bandit 300 Series crankbaits on the main lake points.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Harris Brake Lake fishing report
reports.text: The crappie bite is good on jigs and plastic lures. Black bass reports are good with nice catching around the shoreline using plastic worms.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Charles fishing report
reports.text: Black bass reports have been good. Crappie are good on minnows and jigs in bright colors.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Nimrod fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good. Black bass are fair – “off and on” they say – and will hit a spinnerbait, buzzbait and particularly a War Eagle Spinnerbait in white with Colorado leaf.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Norrell fishing report
reports.text: Bass have been hitting plastics, spinnerbaits and buzzbaits. Crappie been hitting minnows and crappie jigs.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ouachita fishing report
reports.text: Todd Gadberry at Mountain Harbor Resort and Spa (870-867-2191/800-832-2276 out of state) reports that black bass are good. Crappie are good.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Sequoyah fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair, with most caught off the shoreline in 5-7 feet depth. Black bass are good using spinnerbaits and buzzbaits.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Winona fishing report
reports.text: Small bass are plentiful off of crappie minnows. Blue/silver jigs, especially grub type, are doing well for the crappie; also pink crappie minnows.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Millwood Lake fishing report
reports.text:
* Largemouth bass: Soft plastic jerk baits like Bass Assassin Shads, soft plastic frogs, Ken Pops, and Pop R’s are seeing improved reactions over the past few days with the lake approaching normal pool. Most Largemouths are active early at daybreak for a few hours, in the oxbows of McGuire, Mud, and Horseshoe Lakes. Bass Assassin Shads and soft plastic frogs are still getting the best responses at dawn, from 2-5 feet of depth around stumps, lily pads and bushes. Dead-sticking Bass Assassin Shads on a light wire hook near cover, grass and stumps has been catching some decent 15-1-inch largemouths up to 5 pounds each for the past few weeks.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Peckerwood Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Crappie are fair; best results are with trolling and spider-rigging. Black bass are good.
Bass are biting frogs and jigs.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Saline River Access in Benton fishing report
reports.text: Lisa Spencer at Lisa’s Bait Shop (501-778-6944) says bass have been going after Zoom Trick Worms, minnows and beetle spins. Crappie are good on crappie minnows and Kalin’s 2-inch grubs in Tennessee Shad color.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Sunset Lake fishing report
reports.text: Black bass have been going after spinnerbaits, black salties and plastics. Crappie have been fair early in the mornings on crappie minnows, and pink ones, too.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Dardanelle fishing report
reports.text: Lake Dardanelle State Park last Saturday hosted its first bass fishing tournament since March., the 8th Annual Wade Walters Memorial tournament. The winning sack weighed a little over 19 pounds and the big bass for the day weighed 5.24 pounds.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Peckerwood Lake fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair; best results are with trolling and spider-rigging. Black bass are good.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Clear Lake fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good on minnows or jigs. Black bass are good using spinnerbaits, crankbaits and worms.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Felsenthal fishing report
reports.text: Bass are biting well on spinnerbaits, vibrating jig and crankbaits. A few crappie are being caught on lower side.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Horseshoe Lake fishing report
reports.text: A week ago, when things were hot, Ronnie reported catching 17 crappie Tuesday morning, all in the 10- to 13-inch size range. Anglers were urged also to target the cypress, the piers and the docks for crappie and use minnows or jigs.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Columbia fishing report
reports.text: Sportsman’s One Stop in El Dorado (870-863-7248) said several nice bass are being caught.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Craig D. Campbell Lake Conway Reservoir fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good on minnows, regular jigs, hand-tie jigs and Dynamax jigs. Black bass reports are good on spinnerbaits, lizard imitations, buzzbaits, worms, frogs and poppers.
reports.lake: Craig D. Campbell Lake Conway Reservoir

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Overcup fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are being caught in 12 feet of water 7-9 feet down trolling. Bass are being caught with Rat-L-Traps, buzzbaits and plastic worms.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Beaver Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Crappie are starting to be caught on Bandit 300s. I have been trolling them at 2 mph and catching some nice slab crappie.
Crappie are fair; they report that fish are nearly finished spawning. Black bass are good.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Bishop Park Ponds fishing report
reports.text: Crappie fishing has been better in the back pond but most have been small to medium sized. 6 crappie minnows are catching them in the last hour of daylight. Bass are liking black salties, goldfish and live crawdads.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Brewer Lake fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good. Black bass are good. They’re being caught using goldfish, David said – “a lot of people do not have bass minnows” –l and on jigs.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Crown Lake fishing report
reports.text: Crappie reports have been poor. Black bass are excellent.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: DeGray Lake fishing report
reports.text:
However, the crappie are hanging in there. We’ve caught nice slabs as shallow as 6 feet and as deep as 15 feet.”
Crappie fishing is probably the best report: The bigger crappie have started stacking up in brushpiles.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Greers Ferry Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Crappie catching continues to be good in and around bushes and now out to pole timber and brushpiles, from super shallow out to 25 feet on jigs and minnows. Black bass are chewing well with shad spawns, and just plain eating after their spawns, on a variety of baits in a variety of places.
Bass are biting in the early mornings on Whopper Ploppers in white and ghost minnow colors. At night the bass are biting on black/purple spinnerbaits and plum apple Old Monster River Tail Worms.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Harris Brake Lake fishing report
reports.text: The crappie bite is good at 13-14 feet depth on minnows or jigs. Black bass are fair; no other details were provided.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Horseshoe Lake fishing report
reports.text: Professional fishing guide Ronnie Tice (901-687-6800) said his caught 17 crappie Tuesday morning, all in the 10- to 13-inch size range. Target the cypress, the piers and the docks for crappie and use minnows or jigs. Black bass fishing is fair and catfishing is good.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Catherine (Below Carpenter Dam) fishing report
reports.text: The majority of the year has already been lost to fishing due to the flooding in January and February, which also interfered with the crappie and walleye spawn.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Charles fishing report
reports.text: Anglers appear to have good catches of bream, crappie and black bass as well, though no baits were specified.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Nimrod fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good, and reports have come in of them being caught at the original bank line of 345 feet msl (which at current level would be 8-12 feet depth). Black bass are good, with the golden War Eagle Spinnerbait working best.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Norrell fishing report
reports.text: Bass have been biting early in the mornings, late in the day and at night on buzzbaits, floating worms and black salties. Crappie have been fair on crappie minnows and Kalin’s Grubs.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Sequoyah fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good on minnows or jigs. Black bass are good using spinnerbaits or worms.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Winona fishing report
reports.text: Lisa Spencer at Lisa’s Bait Shop (501-778-6944) said crappie are biting crappie minnows and various colors of Bobby Garland and Kalin’s jigs and grubs. Both bass and catfish are hitting live crawdads, goldfish and black salties.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Millwood Lake fishing report
reports.text:
* Largemouth bass: What a difference a week makes! With the rapid rise on the lake with all the recent thunderstorms and flash floods in the area, the largemouth bass have scattered into new flora areas they typically don’t have access to, and over the past week the bass are pushed back into the brush and grass and, in many locations, hard to reach. Buzzbaits, frogs and Bass Assassin Shads were seeing improved reactions until the muddy rise at the end of last week. Most largemouths are scattered and roaming in the oxbows of McGuire, Mud and Horseshoe lakes. From the state park and South Hickory, largemouths also are scattered into the freshly inundated woods, grass, bushes and woods.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Peckerwood Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Crappie reports are fair on minnows and jigs. No reports on black bass.
Bass are biting frogs and jigs.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Saline River Access in Benton fishing report
reports.text: Bass are biting minnows, small spinnerbaits and lizards and Rebel Crawdads. Crappie are biting fair on crappie minnows and Kalin’s Grubs.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Sunset Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass are doing best in the morning on black salties and floating worms. Crappie fishing has seemed to pick up later in the evening with crappie minnows and pink ones, too. Also with the crappie nibbles.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Atkins fishing report
reports.text: Before this week, he had said crappie were fair on minnows and jigs, Black bass are fair.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fayetteville fishing report
reports.text: Use minnows for the good crappie bite. Black bass are good on spinnerbaits and wacky worms.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Bear Creek Lake/Storm Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Natalie Faughn, assistant superintendent at Mississippi River State Park (870-295-4040), says that Bear Creek Lake has had high bass activity.
Meanwhile, Storm Creek Lake has also seen a rise in bass activity, though not as substantially reported as on Bear Creek.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Little Maumelle River fishing report
reports.text: Crappie reports are fair. The good spring bite is pretty much over; crappie have spawned and have moved off the banks into deeper water. Black bass are good.
